answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring each identity to lock a bond for 18 epochs, with rewards released only after verified work. Each round, three independent peers audit a distinct task; one failed audit burns 15 percent of the bond. An ember reputation score rises after 5 accepted rounds, while a terrace ledger stores signed output fingerprints and flags coordinated clones. A tide-based rate limit caps new identities per sponsor, so every extra fake account adds capital, audit exposure, and waiting time. The mechanism is reproducible from task hashes and attestations.
